Resolve closes an open or accepted entry, recording who closed it:

  --note TEXT              fixed; the note says how (a commit, a command)
  --wontfix --note TEXT    not going to change; the note says why
  --dup OTHER_ID           the same as another entry here, whose votes
                           then include this one's (and which takes over
                           its links to other hosts)

Fixed or won't fix, it closes the entries linked to it on other hosts the
same way, over the agent bus, and theirs in turn; --only closes just this
one. A host that can't be reached is listed with what to run: once its bus
answers, --linked passes a closed entry's resolution on to its linked
entries still open.

Usage:
  agent friction resolve <id> (--note TEXT | --wontfix --note TEXT | --dup OTHER_ID | --linked) [flags]

Examples:
  agent friction resolve 12 --note "wait names the last status (abc1234)"
  agent friction resolve 13 --wontfix --note "keys is raw by design; use send"
  agent friction resolve 14 --dup 12
  agent friction resolve 12 --linked

Flags:
      --dup string    Close it as a duplicate of this entry
  -h, --help          help for resolve
      --linked        Pass a closed entry's resolution on to its linked entries
      --note string   How it was fixed, or why it won't be
      --only          Resolve only this entry, not its linked entries on other hosts
      --wontfix       Close it as won't fix

Global Flags:
      --backend string          Backend for spawn or adopt: claude, aider, agy, or shell (spawn requires it or --backend-config; adopt auto-detects)
      --backend-config string   JSON file defining a custom backend (or app settings); pass it again to status/wait/watch for agents spawned with it
  -q, --quiet                   Don't print hints (results and errors still print)
      --termd-ns string         g3d-termd namespace (default: agents; never default or wall)
